Imperial College London · Directed Reading Programme


Financial Econometrics

Can we predict financial market turbulence?
An empirical introduction to financial time series, volatility forecasting and mathematical modelling.




Part I — Financial Time Series


 SESSION 01 Financial Stylised Facts  Prices, returns, distributions and empirical patterns.  
 SESSION 02 Stationarity and Time Series Models  Random walks, ARIMA, GARCH and stochastic simulations.  


Part II — Volatility Forecasting


 SESSION 03 Measuring and Forecasting Volatility  Latent volatility, realised variance and Value-at-Risk.  
 SESSION 04 GARCH Models and Risk Forecasting  Model fitting, conditional variance and backtesting.  
 SESSION 05 HAR Models and Realised Volatility  Volatility persistence across multiple time horizons.  
 SESSION 06 Machine Learning and Volatility Forecasting  Boosted trees, model comparisons and research projects.  


Part III — Continuous-Time Models and Research


 SESSION 07 Continuous-Time Financial Models  Brownian motion, diffusions and Lévy jump processes.  
 SESSION 08 Point Processes and Market Microstructure  Poisson processes, Hawkes models and event clustering.  
 SESSION 09 From Diffusions to Self-Exciting Markets  Connecting continuous-time price dynamics and event arrivals.  
 SESSION 10 Research Workshop  Independent investigations, findings and discussion.
